rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medina, Basra, and Syria's readers and jurists, with Abu Hanifa, hold that the basmala is not a verse of al-Fatiha or other surahs; it separates surahs and is blessed at the opening, so they do not recite it aloud.
rows.anchor: هو مذهب أبي حنيفة ومن تابعه رحمهم الله ولذا لا يجهر بها عندهم في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan and Kufan readers, with al-Shafi'i and his companions, count it as a verse of al-Fatiha and every surah and recite it aloud; they cite its inclusion in the early codices despite the instruction to exclude non-Qur'anic material.
rows.anchor: وقراء مكة والكوفة على أنها آية من الفاتحة ومن كل سورة وعليه الشافعى وأصحابه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that whoever omits the basmala has omitted 114 verses from God's Book.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما من تركها فقد ترك مائة وأربع عشرة آية من كتاب الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A Prophetic report presents al-Fatiha as divided between God and His servant: God answers the praise, glorification, and magnification, shares the response to worship and aid, and grants the servant's request in the closing supplication.
rows.anchor: حديث أبي هريرة قال سمعت النبي عليه السلام يقول قال الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة أي الفاتحة بينى وبين عبدى نصفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report begins God's response when the servant says “Praise belongs to God,” which indicates the basmala is not part of al-Fatiha; if it is outside al-Fatiha, consensus excludes it from other surahs too.
rows.anchor: فالابتداء بقوله الحمد لله دليل على أن التسمية ليست من الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Hanafi account the basmala remains a Qur'anic verse revealed to separate surahs; this does not contradict its exclusion from the surahs themselves.
rows.anchor: التسمية آية من القرآن انزلت للفصل بين السور عندنا ذكره فخر الإسلام في المبسوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial ba attaches to an omitted verb such as “I read” or “I recite”; the act named is understood from the basmala that precedes it, as in a traveler saying it on departure or arrival.
rows.anchor: وتعلقت الباء بمحذوف تقديره بسم الله اقرأ أو أتلو لأن الذى يتلو التسمية مقروء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted verb follows the basmala because the act and its object matter most; placing the divine name first gives it exclusive priority over the polytheists' invocations of al-Lat and al-Uzza.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يبدءون بأسماء آلهتم فيقولون باسم اللات وباسم العزى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “Read in the name of your Lord,” the verb is brought forward because reading was the central command of the first-revealed surah; “read” may also mean perform reading absolutely, or take the following phrase as its object.
rows.anchor: وكان الأمر بالقراءة اهم فكان تقديم الفعل اوقع ويجوز أن يحمل اقرأ على معنى افعل القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ba is kasra-marked because it is invariably a preposition governing genitive; the noun's initial hamza is added only when it begins speech, while medial pronunciation drops it.
rows.anchor: وبنيت الباء على الكسر لأنها تلازم الحرفية والجر فكسرت لتشابه حركتها عملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun ism has a prosthetic hamza for initial pronunciation, can be shortened to sim, and derives from deleted-final form samw, “elevation”: naming raises and publicizes the named one's mention.
rows.anchor: واشتقاقه من السمو وهو الرفعة لأن التسمية تنويه بالمسمى وإشادة بذكره

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz instructed his scribe to lengthen the ba, make the sin strokes clear, and round the mim; the written alif is omitted here through frequent use.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز لكاتبه طول الباء واظهر السينات ودور الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is uniquely the name of the true God, not an attribute; the source derives it from al-ilah with hamza loss, while Khalil, al-Zajjaj, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl deny derivation and other accounts link it to bewilderment or worship.
rows.anchor: والله أصله الإله ونظيره الناس أصله الأناس حذفت الهمزة وعوض منها حرف التعريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām of Allah is generally emphatic after fatḥa or ḍamma and light after kasra; some readers lighten it in every position, others always emphasize it, while the first pattern is the majority practice.
rows.anchor: وتفخم لامه إذا كان قبلها فتحة أو ضمة وترقق إذا كان قبلها كسرة ومنهم من يرققها بكل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman and Rahim are both derived from mercy, but Rahman is more emphatic because it has two augmentative patterns versus one in Rahim; added form signals added meaning.
rows.anchor: وفي الرحمن من المبالغة ما ليس في الرحيم لأن في الرحيم زيادة واحدة وفى الرحمن زيادتين وزيادة اللفظ تدل على زيادة المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman describes mercy encompassing all creation, believer and unbeliever, especially in this world; Rahim describes mercy particular to believers in the hereafter, explaining the supplicatory usage and the order of the names.
rows.anchor: ولذا جاء في الدعاء يارحمن الدنيا لأنه يعم المؤمن والكافر ورحيم الآخرة لأنه يخص المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman is restricted as a name to God but universal in meaning, while Rahim can describe others and is particular in its referent; Rahman is nevertheless placed first despite its greater force.
rows.anchor: وقالوا الرحمن خاص تسمية لأنه لا يوصف به غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hostile poet applied “Rahman” to Musaylima as a taunt in unbelief, not as a genuine divine description.
rows.anchor: وأما قول الشاعر في مسيلمة وأنت غيث الورى لا زلت رحمانا فباب من تعنتهم في كفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians differ on whether Rahman declines: those requiring the absence of a faʿlān feminine form leave it indeclinable, while those requiring a faʿlā feminine form decline it; the first analysis is preferable.
rows.anchor: ورحمن غير منصرف عند من زعم أن الشرط انتفاء فعلانه إذ ليس له فعلانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-hamd is beautiful praise given preferentially; syntactically it is a nominative subject with an implied predicate such as “due” or “established,” while a reading with an implicit verb makes it an accusative verbal noun.
rows.anchor: الوصف الجميل على جهة التفضيل وهو رفع بالابتداء وأصله النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from accusative to nominative indicates that praise is settled and enduring.
rows.anchor: والعدول عن النصب إلى الرفع للدلالة على ثبات المعنى واستقراره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd and madḥ may both mean praising what is beautiful, whether a favor or an inherent quality; shukr is specifically for a favor and uses heart, tongue, and limbs, whereas hamd is praise by tongue alone.
rows.anchor: وأما الشكر فعلى النعمة خاصة وهو بالقلب واللسان والجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poet says favors elicited three forms of gratitude: hand, tongue, and the veiled heart.
rows.anchor: قال أفادتكم النعماء منى ثلاثة يدى ولسانى والضمير المحجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report calls praise the head of gratitude and says a servant has not thanked God without praising Him; verbal mention spreads notice of a favor more than inward belief or ambiguous bodily acts.
rows.anchor: ومنه الحديث الحمد رأس الشكر ما شكر الله عبد لم يحمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative distinction makes madḥ praise inherent perfections, such as power and knowledge, and shukr praise for benefactions; hamd covers both.
rows.anchor: وقيل المدح ثناء على ما هو له من أوصاف الكمال ككونه باقيا قادرا عالما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-hamd is exhaustive according to the author's school, against the Mu'tazila; joining it to Allah's proper name gathers every perfection and rests on the doctrine of created acts.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام فيه للاستغراق عندنا خلافا للمعتزلة ولذا قرن باسم الله لأنه اسم ذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb means owner or master; the source cites Safwan telling Abu Sufyan that being ruled by a Quraysh man is preferable to being ruled by a Hawazin man, and allows “rabb” as an intensive verbal noun.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول صفوان لأبي سفيان لأن يربنى رجل من قريش أحب إلى من أن يربنى رجل من هوازن

rows.speaker: الواسطى
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti explains Rabb as creator at the beginning, sustainer through nourishment, and forgiver at the end, and calls it God's greatest name.
rows.anchor: وقال الواسطى هو الخالق ابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb is used without qualification only for God; human use requires a restriction, as in the cited accounts of Joseph.
rows.anchor: ولم يطلقوا الرب إلا في الله وحده وهو فى العبد مع التقيد إنه ربى أحسن مثواى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿālamīn denotes what makes the Creator known—bodies, substances, and accidents—or every existent apart from God; its sound masculine plural reflects a descriptive quality associated with rational beings.
rows.anchor: والعالم هو ما علم به الخالق من الأجسام والجواهر والأعراض أوكل موجود سوى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating Rahman and Rahim here supports the conclusion that the basmala is not part of al-Fatiha, since repetition would otherwise add no information.
rows.anchor: ذكرهما قد مر وهو دليل على أن التسمية ليست من الفاتحة إذ لو كانت منها لما أعادهما لخلو الاعادة عن الافادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asim reads Mālik, while the others read Malik; some prefer Malik because it needs no genitive construction, fits “To whom belongs sovereignty today?”, every king owns but not every owner is king, and a king's command governs an owner.
rows.anchor: عاصم وعلى ملك غيرهما وهو الاختيار عند البعض لاستغنائه عن الاضافة ولقوله لمن الملك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view gives Mālik greater reward because it has more letters; Abu Hanifa and al-Hasan are reported to read Malik.
rows.anchor: وقيل المالك اكثر ثوابا لأنه أكثر حروفا وقرأ أبو حنيفة والحسن رضى الله عنهما ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm al-din means the day of recompense, as in the saying that one is repaid as one acts.
rows.anchor: يوم الجزاء ويقال كما تدين تدان أي كما تفعل تجازى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive construction with “day” is an expanded use of an active participle with a temporal adverb; God owns all affairs on the day of judgment, when authority belongs to Him alone.
rows.anchor: اى مالك الأمر كله فى يوم الدين والتخصيص بيوم الدين لأن الأمر فيه لله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The participle can modify a definite noun because its genitive is treated as genuine when it denotes continuing ownership; these descriptions establish that none but God deserves praise.
rows.anchor: لأنه أريد به الاستمرار فكانت الاضافة حقيقة فساغ أن يكون صفة للمعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats iya as a detached pronoun and the kaf as an address particle without syntactic position; al-Khalil treats iya as the pronoun with the kaf attached to it.
rows.anchor: ايا عند الخليل وسيبويه اسم مضمر والكاف حرف خطاب عند سيبويه ولا محل له من الاعراب

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans treat the whole form iyaka as one pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقال الكوفيون إياك بكمالها اسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the object marks exclusivity: worship and the seeking of aid are directed to God alone; worship is the utmost submission and abasement.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المفعول لقصد الاختصاص والمعنى نخصك بالعبادة وهى أقصى غاية الخضوع والتذلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person reference to direct address is iltifat; Arabic rhetoric uses such shifts to refresh attention and heighten reception, and the cited Qur'anic and poetic examples illustrate its forms.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن الغيبة إلى الخطاب للالتفات وهو قد يكون من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ومن الخطاب إلى الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Direct address follows the great descriptions of God: the one worthy of praise, humility, and aid is addressed as the uniquely distinguished Lord described above.
rows.anchor: أنه لما ذكر الحقيق بالحمد والثناء وأجرى عليه تلك الصفات العظام تعلق العلم بمعلوم عظيم الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship precedes asking for aid because presenting the means before a request brings a response closer; alternatively, the order follows the preceding arrangement of the verses.
rows.anchor: وقدمت العبادة على الاستعانة لأن تقديم الوسيلة قبل طلب الحاجة أقرب إلى الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for aid is unrestricted and covers every need; alternatively it asks for God's help and enabling grace in performing acts of worship, which the following request for guidance specifies.
rows.anchor: وأطلقت الاستعانة لتنناول كل مستعان فيه ويجوز أن يراد الاستعانة به وبتوفيقه على أداء العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Guide us” can mean keep us firm on the clear way, like telling someone already standing to remain there, or guide us henceforth as You have guided us already.
rows.anchor: أي ثبتنا على المنهاج الواضح كقولك للقائم قم حتى أعود إليك اى اثبت على ما أنت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hada can govern one object directly or govern another with the particles li and ila, as the cited verses show.
rows.anchor: وهدى يتعدى بنفسه إلى مفعول واحد فأما تعديه إلى مفعول آخر فقد جاء متعديا إليه بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat is the road, from the root for swallowing, as if it swallows travelers who walk it.
rows.anchor: والسراط الجادة من سرط الشئ إذا ابتلعه كأنه يسرط السابلة إذا سلكوه

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads the initial consonant as a sound between ṣād and zāy, assimilated toward the emphatic ṭāʾ.
rows.anchor: وهى قراءة حمزة والسين قراءة ابن كثير

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads sirat with sīn throughout the Qur'an; the source calls this the word's original form.
rows.anchor: والسين قراءة ابن كثير فى كل القرآن وهى الأصل فى الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use pure ṣād, the Quraysh dialect and the form fixed in the codex; sirat can be masculine or feminine and here means Islam's path of truth.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالصاد الخالصة وهى لغة قريش وهى الثابتة فى المصحف الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The path of those You favored” is an appositive restating the straight path, both reinforcing the point and identifying it as the Muslims' path; this emphatically attests to its uprightness.
rows.anchor: بدل من الصراط وهو فى حكم تكرير العامل وفائدته التأكيد والإشعار بأن الصراط المستقيم تفسيره صراط المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those favored are the believers and prophets, or the people of Moses before they changed.
rows.anchor: وهم المؤمنون والأنبياء عليهم السلام أو قوم موسى قبل أن يغيروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Other than those under anger” is an appositive: those favored are the ones spared God's anger and misguidance.
rows.anchor: بدل من الذين أنعمت عليهم يعنى أن المنعم عليهم هم الذين سلموا من غضب الله والضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase qualifies the favored, who combine the full blessing of faith with safety from divine anger and error; the source explains why “other than” can qualify a definite antecedent.
rows.anchor: أو صفة للذين يعنى أنهم جمعوا بين النعمة المطلقة وهى نعمة الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first “upon them” is an object and the second is a subject; God's anger means His will to exact revenge and impose punishment on deniers.
rows.anchor: وعليهم الأولى محلها النصب على المفعولية ومحل الثانية الرفع على الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported identification takes those under anger as Jews, citing the verse about those God cursed and angered.
rows.anchor: وقيل المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود لقوله تعالى من لعنه الله وغضب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported identification takes the astray as Christians, citing the verse that says they went astray before.
rows.anchor: والضالون هم النصارى لقوله تعالى قد ضلوا من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basran grammarians take la as emphatic negation; Kufans take it to mean “other than.”
rows.anchor: ولا زائدة عند البصريين للتوكيد وعند الكوفيين هى بمعنى غير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked about Amin, Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet explained it as “respond” or “so be it”; the word is a built verbal noun with long and short vowel forms.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن معنى آمين فقال افعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet's evidence shows both long and short forms of Amin, and a Prophetic report says Gabriel taught Amin at the end of al-Fatiha, like a seal on a letter; it is not Qur'an because codices omit it.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام لقننى جبريل آمين عند فراغى من قراءة فاتحة الكتاب وقال إنه كالختم على الكتاب

none: Surah heading and basmala only; no commentary point.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means declare God's essence free of what does not befit Him; “name” is an extra word and “Most High” denotes dominion and power, not location.
rows.anchor: نزه ذاته عما لا يليق به والاسم صلة وذلك بأن يفسر الأعلى بمعنى العلو الذى هو القهر والافتدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative is to say “Glory be to my Lord Most High”; a report says that when this verse descended the Prophet instructed worshippers to use it in prostration.
rows.anchor: وقيل قل سبحان ربى الأعلى وفى الحديث لما نزلت قال علية السلام اجعلوها فى سجودكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created everything and fashioned it harmoniously, not unevenly or incoherently, with order and evidence of a knowing, wise source; alternatively, He fashioned each thing for its benefit and good.
rows.anchor: أى خلق كل شئ فسوى خلقه تسوية ولم يأت به متفاوتا غير ملتئم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God allotted each animal what benefits it, guided it to that provision, and taught it how to use it.
rows.anchor: أى قدرلكل حيوان ما يصلحه فهداه إليه وعرفه وجه الانتفاع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “guided” implies both guiding and leading astray, with the latter omitted by ellipsis as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: أو فهدى وأضل ولكن حذف وأضل اكتفاء كقوله يضل من يشاء ويهدى من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pasture is what God caused to grow for animals to graze.
rows.anchor: أنبت ما ترعاه الدواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the pasture dry and brittle refuse; ahwa means black and grammatically qualifies the refuse.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أحوى ﴾ أسود فأحوى صفة لغثاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means what God chooses to abrogate: God assures the Prophet that revelation will remain preserved except what He removes from memory by lifting its ruling and recitation.
rows.anchor: أن ينسخه وهذا بشارة من الله لبنيه أن يحفظ عليه الوحى حتى لا ينفلت منه شئ

rows.speaker: جنيد
rows.claim: When Ibn Kaysan asked Junayd about “you will not forget,” Junayd interpreted it as not forgetting to act upon the revelation.
rows.anchor: وسأل ابن كيسان النحوى جنيدا عنه فقال فلا تنسى العمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading treats “you will not forget” as a prohibition, with an added final alif for rhyme; it means do not repeat the recitation until you forget it, except what God causes you to forget by lifting its recitation.
rows.anchor: وقيل قوله فلا تنسى على النهى والألف مزيدة للفاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the Prophet's audible recitation alongside Gabriel and the inward fear of forgetting; alternatively He knows hidden and public speech, deeds, and states.
rows.anchor: أى إنك تجهر بالقراءة مع قراءة جبريل مخافة التفلت والله يعلم جهرك معه وما فى نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause is coordinated with “We shall make you recite”; the preceding clause is an aside, and the meaning is that God will enable the easier way of preserving revelation.
rows.anchor: معطوف على سنقرئك وقوله انه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى اعتراض ومعناه ونوفقك للطريقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations take the easier way as the lenient revealed law or as enabling the Prophet to perform the deeds of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل للشريعة السمحة التى هى أيسر الشرائع أو توفقك لعمل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means admonish people with the Qur'an; the following conditional can be read as expressing the improbability that admonition will affect them.
rows.anchor: عظ بالقرآن ﴿ إن نفعت الذكرى ﴾ جواب ان مدلول قوله فذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command to admonish is unconditional, like the explicit statement that the Prophet is only an admonisher.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو أمر بالتذكير على الاطلاق كقوله فذكر إنما أنت مذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who fears God and a bad end will soon take heed and accept the reminder.
rows.anchor: ﴿ سيذكر ﴾ سيتعظ ويقبل التذكرة ﴿ من يخشى ﴾ الله وسوء العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched person turns away from the reminder and does not accept it.
rows.anchor: ويتباعد عن الذكرى فلا يقبلها ﴿ الأشقى ﴾ الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Most wretched” may mean an unbeliever generally or the most deeply unbelieving because of his intense hostility to the Messenger; it is said to have been revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Utba ibn Rabi'a.
rows.anchor: الكافر أو الذى هو أشقى الكفر لتوغله فى عداوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قيل نزلت فى الوليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He enters the great Fire, identified as Hell; the lesser fire is the fire of this world.
rows.anchor: يدخل نار جهنم والصغرى نار الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Hell he neither dies and escapes torment nor lives a pleasurable life.
rows.anchor: فيستريح من العذاب ﴿ ولا يحيى ﴾ حياة يتلذذ بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word “then” indicates that the suspended state between life and death is even more dreadful than entering the Fire, so it comes later in severity.
rows.anchor: وقيل ثم لأن الترجح بين الحياة والموت أفظع من الصلى فهو متراخ عنه فى مراتب الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A successful person attains victory; “purifies himself” can mean becoming free of shirk, purifying oneself through prayer, or paying alms, by analogy with charity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قد أفلح ﴾ نال الفوز ﴿ من تزكى ﴾ نطهر من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering the Lord's name means saying the opening takbir and then performing the five prayers.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وذكر اسم ربه ﴾ وكبر للافتتاح ﴿ فصلى ﴾ الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is evidence that the opening takbir is obligatory, distinct from the prayer because prayer is coordinated with it, and may use any of God's names.
rows.anchor: وبه يحتج على وجوب تكبيرة الافتتاح وعلى أنها ليست من الصلاة لأن الصلاة عطفت عليها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets remembrance as recalling the return and standing before one's Lord, followed by prayer to Him.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدى ربه فصلى له

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets remembrance as invoking God's name on the way to the prayer place, followed by the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك وذكر اسم ربه فى طريق المصلى فصلى صلاة العيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees prefer worldly life over the hereafter and therefore fail to do what brings success; the addressees are unbelievers.
rows.anchor: على الآخرة فلا تفعلون ما به تفلحون والمخاطب به الكافرون

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads the verb in the third-person plural, “they prefer,” supporting the identification of the addressees as unbelievers.
rows.anchor: دليله قراءة أبى عمرو يؤثرون بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hereafter is better in its own right and more enduring.
rows.anchor: أفضل فى نفسها وأدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This” points either to the statements that the successful person is purified and the hereafter is better, or to the whole surah; these meanings are present in the earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: هذا إشارة إلى قوله قد أفلح إلى أبقى أى أن معنى هذا الكلام وأراد فى تلك الصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that this Qur'anic teaching is in earlier scriptures, despite different wording and language, supports the permissibility of reciting the Qur'an in Persian during prayer.
rows.anchor: وهو دليل على جواز قراءة القرآن بالفارسية فى الصلاة لأنه جعله مذكورا فى تلك الصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The earlier scriptures” is specified by apposition as the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
rows.anchor: بدل من الصحف الاولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An aphorism attributed to Abraham's scriptures says a wise person should guard his tongue, know his time, and attend to his own affairs.
rows.anchor: وفى الأثر وفى صحف إبراهيم ينبغى للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative means “has indeed come”; the overwhelming event is the catastrophe of the Resurrection that envelops people in hardship and terror.
rows.anchor: ﴿ هل ﴾ بمعنى قد ﴿ أتاك حديث الغاشية ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the overwhelming event is Hell, as in the verse saying that the Fire covers their faces.
rows.anchor: وقيل النار من قوله وتغشى وجوههم النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces are those of unbelievers, singled out because deep grief or joy marks a person's face; they are abject on the day of the overwhelming event through humiliation and disgrace.
rows.anchor: أى وجوه الكفار وإنما خص الوجه لأن الحزن والسرور إذا استحكما فى المرء أثرا فى وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the people toil in Hell dragging chains and shackles, wading through fire as through mud, and continually climbing and descending its slopes.
rows.anchor: تعمل فى النار عملا تتعب فيه وهو جرها السلاسل والاغلال وخوضها فى النار كما تخوض الابل فى الوحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says they did evil deeds in worldly life, enjoyed them, and now suffer their consequences in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: وقيل عملت فى الدنيا أعمال السوء والتذت بها وتنعمت فهى فى نصب منها فى الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view identifies the people as monastics who humbled themselves and labored in fasting and constant night prayer, yet face punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم أصحاب الصوامع ومعناه أنها خشعت لله وعملت ونصبت فى أعمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They enter a fire heated for a long time, whose heat has no equal; Abu Amr and Abu Bakr read the verb with the specified form.
rows.anchor: تدخل نارا قد أحميت مددا طويلة فلا حر يعدل حرها تصلى أبو عمرو وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are given water from a spring whose heat has reached its utmost; feminine forms refer to the faces while meaning their owners.
rows.anchor: من عين ماء قد انتهى حرها والتأنيث فى هذه الصفات والافعال راجعة إلى الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dari' is a plant called shibriq that becomes dari' when dry and is deadly poison; Hell's inmates are in different classes, so this does not conflict with the verse limiting food to ghislin.
rows.anchor: وهو نبت يقال له الشبرق فإذا يبس فهو ضريع وهو سم قاتل والعذاب ألوان والمعذبون طبقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is genitive as an adjective of dari'; the two benefits of food, removing hunger and adding bodily weight, are absent.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لا يسمن ﴾ مجرور المحل لأنه وصف ضريع ﴿ ولا يغني من جوع ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage now describes the faces of believers; it restarts with “faces” rather than coordinating with the earlier phrase because that discussion had grown long and ended; they enjoy a gentle life.
rows.anchor: ثم وصف وجوه المؤمنين ولم يقل ووجوه لأن الكلام الأول قد طال وانقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are pleased with their deeds and obedience when they see the honor and reward those deeds earned.
rows.anchor: رضيت بعملها وطاعتها لما رأت ما أداهم اليه من الكرامة والثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The high garden may be elevated in physical location or in rank.
rows.anchor: من علو المكان أو المقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb may address the listener or the faces; laġiya can mean idle talk, a person who speaks idly, or a soul that engages in idle speech, and the garden's speech is wisdom and praise.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لا تسمع ﴾ يا مخاطب أو الوجوه ﴿ فيها لاغية ﴾

rows.speaker: مكى وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Meccan and Abu Amr recite “one does not hear idle speech there,” rather than “you do not hear.”
rows.anchor: لا يسمع فيها لاغية مكى وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafi recites the feminine second-person form, “you do not hear idle speech there.”
rows.anchor: ولا تسمع فيها لاغية نافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular spring denotes many springs, as in the expression that each soul knew what it did.
rows.anchor: أى عيون كثيرة كقوله علمت نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The couches are elevated in rank or height, allowing a seated believer to see all the kingdom and blessings God has granted.
rows.anchor: من رفعة المقدار أو السمك ليرى المؤمن بجلوسه عليه جميع ما خوله ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cups are drinking vessels; alternatively, they are vessels without handles. They are placed before the inhabitants for delight in their sight or beside springs ready for drinking.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأكواب ﴾ جمع كوب وهو القدح وقيل آنية لا عروة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cushions are arranged side by side, so wherever a person sits there is one to sit on and another to lean against.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ونمارق ﴾ وسائد ﴿ مصفوفة ﴾ بعضها إلى جنب بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarabi are broad, fine carpets, either spread out or dispersed around the seating places.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وزرابي ﴾ وبسط عراض فاخرة جمع زربية ﴿ مبثوثة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When unbelievers objected that the vast couches, countless cups, long cushions, and broad carpets were unlike anything in worldly life, God answered by directing them to familiar created examples.
rows.anchor: أنكر الكفار وقالوا كيف يصعد على هذا السرير وكيف تكثر الاكواب هذه الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel kneels for loading or mounting and then rises, so the heavenly couch can bend down for a believer as a camel does.
rows.anchor: طويلة ثم تبرك حتى تركب أو تحمل عليها ثم تقوم فكذا السرير يطأطئ المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is raised high without supports; its innumerable stars show how cups could be too numerous for human reckoning.
rows.anchor: رفعا بعيد الذى بلا امساك وعمد ثم نجومها تكثر هذه الكثرة فلا تدخل فى حساب الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains stand firmly without leaning despite their height, just as the cushions can be long.
rows.anchor: نصبا ثابتا فهى راسخة لا تميل مع طولها فكذا النمارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is leveled and made into a single carpet extending horizon to horizon, illustrating the broad carpets of Paradise.
rows.anchor: سطحا بتمهيد وتوطئة فهى كلها بساط واحد تنبسط من الافق إلى الافق فكذا الزرابى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four familiar created things also prove the Creator's power, resurrection, and the truth of the Messenger; Arabs are directed to what they commonly see in the desert, especially the useful and remarkable camel.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى أفلا ينظرون إلى هذه المخلوقات الشاهدة على قدرة الخالق حتى لا ينكروا اقتداره على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to remind people of the evidence so that they reflect; his duty is only to convey the message.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فذكر ﴾ فذكرهم بالادلة ليتفكروا فيها ﴿ إنما أنت مذكر ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musayṭir means one who compels or controls; the verse has a reading with ṣād by the Medinese, Basrans, Ali, and Asim.
rows.anchor: بمسلط كقوله وما أنت عليهم بجبار بمصيطر مدنى وبصرى وعلى وعاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected: the Prophet is not responsible for controlling them, but God has authority and power over those who turn away and disbelieve, and punishes them in Hell.
rows.anchor: الاستثناء منقطع أى لست بمسئول عليهم ولكن من تولى منهم وكفر بالله فإن لله الولاية عليه والقهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the exception attaches to “remind”: remind everyone except those whose faith is no longer expected, who have turned away and earned the greater punishment; the intervening material is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو استثناء من قوله فذكر أى فذكر إلا من انقطع طمعك من إيمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their return is to God; placing “to Us” first intensifies the warning and stresses that they return only to the All-Powerful Avenger.
rows.anchor: رجوعهم وفائدة تقديم الظرف التشديد فى الوعيد وأن ايابهم ليس إلا إلى الجبار المقتدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will reckon their deeds and repay them accordingly; “upon Us” intensifies the threat and does not mean that anything is obligatory upon God.
rows.anchor: فـنحاسبهم على أعمالهم ونجازيهم بها جزاء أمثالهم وعلى لتأكيد الوعيد لا الوجوب اذ لا يجب على الله شئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten nights may be the first ten of Dhu al-Hijja, the first ten of Muharram, or the last ten of Ramadan; they are indefinite to signal their special merit.
rows.anchor: عشر ذى الحجة أو العشر الأول من المحرم أو الآخر من رمضان وإنما نكرت لزيادة فضيلتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The even and odd may mean even and odd things generally, the even and odd nights just named, paired and odd prayers, the tenth day of sacrifice and ninth day of Arafat, or creation and Creator.
rows.anchor: شفع كل الأشياء ووترها أو شفع هذه الليالى ووترها أو شفع الصلاة ووترها

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza and Ali read watr with fatḥa; the others read it with kasra, two dialect forms, the first Hijazi and the second Tamimi.
rows.anchor: والوتر حمزة وعلى بفتح الواو غيرهما وهما لغتان فالفتح حجازى والكسر تميمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Have you not seen?” asks the Prophet to know with certainty comparable to sight; Iram is a clarifying apposition naming the ancient first Ad, by their ancestor, distinct from later Ad.
rows.anchor: أى ألم تعلم يا محمد علما يوازى العيان فى الايقان وهو استفهام تقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Iram is the town or land of Ad; Ibn al-Zubayr's genitive reading supports this, with the implied phrase “the people of Iram.”
rows.anchor: وقيل ارم بلدتهم وأرضهم التى كانوا فيها ويدل عليه قراءة ابن الزبير بعاد ارم على الاضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “possessing pillars” describes the tribe, it means they were nomads with tents or exceptionally tall bodies like pillars; if it describes the town, it means it had columns.
rows.anchor: وذات العماد إذا كانت صفة للقبيلة فالمعنى أنهم كانوا بدويين أهل عمد أو طوال الاجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Shaddad founded a vast jeweled city of Iram in the deserts of Aden; a heavenly cry killed him and his people as they approached it.
rows.anchor: روى أنه كان لعاد ابنان شداد وشديد فملكا وقهرا ثم مات شديد وخلص الأمر لشداد

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن قلابة
rows.claim: Ibn Qilaba says he stumbled on Iram while searching for camels, took what he could, and later recounted the discovery to Muawiya.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن قلانة أنه خرج فى طلب ابل له فوقع عليها فحمل ما قدر عليه

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b identifies the city as Iram and predicts a short, reddish-blond Muslim with moles who will enter it while searching for camels; he identifies Ibn Qilaba as that man.
rows.anchor: وبلغ خبر معاوية فاستحضره فقص عليه فبعث إلى كعب فسأله فقال هى ارم ذات العماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unmatched comparison may be Ad in their strength and stature, with men said to be four hundred cubits tall, or the unmatched city of Shaddad.
rows.anchor: أى مثل عاد فى قوتهم وطول قامتهم كان طول الرجل منهم أربعمائة ذراع أو لم يخلق مثل مدينة شداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud cut houses into mountain rock; a report says they were the first to hollow mountains and built 1,700 stone cities; the valley is Wadi al-Qura.
rows.anchor: قطعوا صخر الجبال واتخذوا فيها بيوتا قيل أول من تحت الجبال والصخور ثمود وبنوا ألفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Possessor of stakes” may mean Pharaoh had numerous troops and tents, or stakes with which he tortured people, as with Asiya.
rows.anchor: أى ذى الجنود الكثيرة وكانت لهم مضارب كثيرة يضربونها إذا نزلوا وقيل كان له أوتاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun can be accusative as censure, nominative as an implied “they are,” or genitive as a description of Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh; they transgressed in the lands.
rows.anchor: فى محل النصب على الذم أو الرفع على هم الذين أو الجر على وصف المذكورين عاد وثمود وفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their corruption consisted of unbelief, killing, and injustice.
rows.anchor: بالكفر والقتل والظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Poured a whip of punishment” is a metaphor for imposing punishment with utmost force: pouring suggests continuity and whip suggests added pain.
rows.anchor: مجاز عن ايقاع العذاب بهم على أبلغ الوجود إذا الصب يشعر بالدوام والسواط بزيادة الايلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The watchpost is the place where watchers await; it portrays God's surveillance, from which people cannot escape, and His knowledge and recording of their deeds for fitting recompense.
rows.anchor: وهو المكان الذى يترقب فيه الرصد مفعال من رصده وهذا مثل لارصاده العباد وانهم لا يفوتونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person wrongly treats abundance as honor and restricted provision as humiliation; God tests with wealth to see gratitude and with poverty to see patience, while the person seeks only immediate pleasure.
rows.anchor: وهو قد عكس فإنه إذا امتحنه ربه بالنعمة والسعة ليشكر قال ربى أكرمنى أى فضلنى بما أعطانى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading qaddara is attributed to the Syrian readers and Yazid and means God constricted provision until it sufficed for subsistence.
rows.anchor: أى ضيق عليه وجعله بمقدار بلغته فقدر شامى ويزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and poverty do not constitute honor or humiliation: honor lies in being enabled to obey, while humiliation lies in abandonment; both conditions are tests of gratitude or patience.
rows.anchor: أى ليس الاكرام والاهانة فى كثرة المال وقلته بل الإكرام فى توفيق الطاعة والاهانة فى الخذلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported “My Lord honored me” is rejected because the speaker claims deserved distinction, whereas God gave wealth as a test without any entitlement; the syntax makes “he says” the predicate and treats each “when” clause as delayed.
rows.anchor: وإنما أنكر قوله ربى أكرمن مع أنه أثبته بقوله فأكرمه لأنه قاله على قصد خلاف ما صححه الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two conditions are both called tests: God tests whether abundance elicits gratitude and whether restricted provision elicits patience, as in the cited verse about testing with good and evil.
rows.anchor: وسمى كلا الأمرين من بسط الرزق وتقديره ابتلاء لأن كل واحد منهما أختيار للعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A greater fault than their mistaken claim about wealth is that they fail to honor or kindly support the vulnerable orphan, and do not urge one another to feed the poor.
rows.anchor: بل هناك شر من هذا القول وهو أن الله يكرمهم بالغنى فلا يؤدون ما يلزمهم فيه من اكرام اليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turath means inheritance; “devouring greedily” means combining lawful and unlawful shares, as they excluded women and children from inheritance and consumed their portions with their own.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وتأكلون التراث ﴾ أى الميراث ﴿ أكلا لما ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs “love” and “love greatly” are equivalent in sense; the phrase indicates intense, greedy love of wealth and withholding its obligations, with variant readings noted for the surrounding verbs.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وتحبون المال ﴾ يقال حبه وأحبه بمعنى ﴿ حبا جما ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke restrains them from their conduct, then warns of their regret when the earth is shaken and repeatedly crushed until it becomes scattered dust.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كلا ﴾ ردع لهم عن ذلك وانكار لفعلهم ثم أتى بالوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's “coming” represents the appearance of the signs of His power and the effects of His sovereignty, as a king's own arrival displays majesty beyond his entourage.
rows.anchor: تمثيل لظهور آيات اقتداره وتبيين آثار قهره وسلطانه فإنه واحدا من الملوك إذا حضر بنفسه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets “your Lord came” as His command and judgment.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس امره وقضاؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels descend from each heaven and form rank after rank, surrounding jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: أى ينزل ملائكة كل سماء فيصطفون صفا بعد صف محدقين بالجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one else administers God's punishment on that day because authority over punishment belongs to God alone.
rows.anchor: أى لا يتولى عذاب الله أحد لأن الأمر لله وحده فى ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشف
rows.claim: The source cites Sahib al-Kashf: no one punishes as severely as God and no one binds as tightly as He does.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب الكشف لا يعذب أحدا حد كعذاب الله ولا يوثق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading attributed to the Prophet and later adopted by Abu Amr at the end of his life takes the pronoun as the human being described, an unbeliever—identified by some as Ubayy ibn Khalaf—whose punishment and fettering no one can match.
rows.anchor: وهى قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ورجع اليها أبو عمرو فى آخر عمره والضمير يرجع إلى الانسان الموصوف وهو الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God addresses the soul to honor it, as He addressed Moses, or an angel speaks on God's behalf; the tranquil soul is secure from fear and grief or settled in certainty.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يا أيتها النفس ﴾ اكراما له كما كلم موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu's reading “O secure and tranquil soul” supports the first interpretation; the address may occur at death, resurrection, or entry into Paradise.
rows.anchor: قراءة أبى يا أيتها النفس الآمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Return to your Lord” can mean return to His promise or reward; the soul is pleased with what God gives and accepted by God for what it has done.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ارجعي إلى ﴾ موعد ﴿ ربك ﴾ أو ثواب ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul joins the company of God's righteous servants and enters their ranks.
rows.anchor: فى جملة عبادى الصالحين فانتظمى فى سلكهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda explains “enter among My servants” as entering with them or among God's chosen servants.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة أى مع عبادى أوبين عبادى أى خواصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the soul as the spirit, entering the bodies of God's servants, supported by Ibn Masud's reading “into My servant's body.”
rows.anchor: وقيل النفس الروح ومعناه فادخلى فى أجسام عبادى كقراءة عبد الله بن مسعود فى جسد عبدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says a strange bird entered Ibn Abbas's bier at his death in Taif and this verse was recited at his grave, though the reciter was unknown.
rows.anchor: ولما مات بن عباس بالطائف جاء طائر لم ير على خلقته فدخل فى نعشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is said to concern Hamza or Khubayb ibn Adi; in a report, God turned Khubayb's face toward the qibla after his prayer and no one could turn it back.
rows.anchor: قيل نزلت فى حمزة بن عبد المطلب وقيل فى خبيب بن عدى الذى صلبه أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse applies generally to believers because the lesson follows the general wording rather than a particular occasion.
rows.anchor: وقيل هى عامة فى المؤمنين إذ العبرة لعموم اللفظ لا لخصوص السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by the sacred city and the following objects that the human being is immersed in arduous struggle; an intervening clause separates oath from its answer.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لا أقسم بهذا البلد ﴾ أقسم سبحانه بالبلد الحرام وبما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the Prophet's being “lawful” in Mecca as part of the hardship: despite his sanctity, his enemies treated him as they treated game outside the sanctuary; it consoles him and marvels at their hostility.
rows.anchor: أى ومن المكابدة ان مثلك على عظم حرمتك يستحل بهذا البلد يعنى مكة كما يستحل الصيد فى غير الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “lawful” points to the future conquest: God promises that the Prophet will be free to do as he wills in Mecca, which had never been made lawful for anyone before; he captured Ibn Khatal and others and protected Abu Sufyan's home.
rows.anchor: أى وأنت حل به فى المستقبل تصنع فيه ما تريده من القتل والاسر وذلك ان الله تعالى فتح عليه مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future reading is confirmed because the surah is unanimously Meccan and its revelation preceded the conquest by years, as in the future-oriented wording “you will die.”
rows.anchor: وكفاك دليلا على أنه للاستقبال أن السورة مكية بالاتفاق وأين الهجرة من وقت نزولها فما بال الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parent and child may be Adam and his descendants, every parent and child, or Abraham and his descendants; ma can mean “who” or “that which.”
rows.anchor: هما آدم وولده أو كل والد وولده أو إبراهيم وولده وما بمعنى من أو بمعنى الذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to a Quraysh notable whom the Messenger endured; some identify him as Abu al-Ashadd or al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. He thinks no resurrection or reckoning can overcome his worldly strength.
rows.anchor: والضمير فى ﴿ أيحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد ﴾ لبعض صناديد قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lubad means much, from a mass or heap; the boast concerns abundant spending on what pre-Islamic Arabs called noble deeds and honors.
rows.anchor: أى كثيرا جمع لبدة وهو ما تلبد أى كثروا جتمع يريد كثرة ما أنفقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He assumes no one saw his spending, which he did ostentatiously for reputation; God saw it and watched over him.
rows.anchor: حين كان ينفق ما ينفق رياه وافتخارا يعنى أن الله تعالى كان يراه وكان عليه رقيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave him two eyes with which to see visible things.
rows.anchor: يبصر بهما المرئيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tongue expresses what is inward; the lips cover the mouth and help with speech, eating, drinking, and blowing.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولسانا ﴾ يعبر به عما فى ضميره ﴿ وشفتين ﴾ يستر بهما ثغره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two paths are the ways of good and evil leading to Paradise and Hell; another view takes them as the two breasts.
rows.anchor: طريقى الخير والشر المفضيين إلى الجنة والنار وقيل الثديين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described by the preceding virtues are the people of the right.
rows.anchor: أ ى الموصوفون بهذه الصفات من أصحاب الميمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs may mean the Qur'an or God's proofs; the people of the left are those of the left hand, or the ill-omened, whose misfortune rests on themselves.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والذين كفروا بآياتنا ﴾ بالقرآن أو بدلائلنا ﴿ هم أصحاب المشأمة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mu'sada means shut and sealed, from the verbs meaning to close; Abu Amr, Hamza, and Hafs read it with hamza.
rows.anchor: أى مطبقة من أوصدت الباب وآصدته إذا أطبقته وأغلقته والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes ma a verbal noun: God's building, spreading, and fashioning creation beautifully. The author rejects this because it disrupts the syntax with the following clause.
rows.anchor: وما مصدرية فى ﴿ والسماء وما بناها والأرض وما طحاها ونفس وما سواها ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred analysis makes ma relative, describing the mighty Creator who built the sky and the wise One who fashioned the soul; the soul is singled out as Adam's or left indefinite to signify all souls or abundance.
rows.anchor: والوجه أن تكون موصولة وانما أو ثرت على من لارادة معنى الوصفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the soul understand obedience and disobedience and recognize that one is good and the other bad.
rows.anchor: فأعلمها طاعتها ومعصيتها أى أفهمها أن أحدهما حسن والآخر قبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The successful one who purifies it” may be the answer to the oath, with an implied emphatic laam, as al-Zajjaj explains.
rows.anchor: جواب القسم والتقدير لقد أفلح قال الزجاج صار طول الكلام عوضا عن اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More plausibly, the oath's answer is omitted: God will destroy the Meccans for rejecting the Messenger as He destroyed Thamud for rejecting Salih; the purification statement is an aside extending the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: وقيل الجواب محذوف وهو الاظهر تقديره ليدمدمن من الله عليهم أى على أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification means God cleansed, set right, and made the soul pure.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من زكاها ﴾ طهرها الله وأصلحها وجعلها زاكية

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the soul purified by God succeeds and the soul God led astray fails.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة أفلحت نفس زكاها الله وخابت نفس أغواها الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the human being performs purification and concealment: concealment is reduction and hiding through sin; the root dassa is originally doubled sīn, with yāʾ replacing one.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون التدسية والتطهير فعل العبدو التدسية والنقص والاخفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud denied because of their transgression, which drove them to denial.
rows.anchor: بطغيانها إذا لحامل لهم على التكذيب طغيانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event occurred when the most wretched man, Qudar ibn Salif, rose to hamstring the she-camel; the time phrase can attach to “denied” or “transgression.”
rows.anchor: ﴿ إذ انبعث ﴾ حين قام بعقر الناقة ﴿ أشقاها ﴾ أشقى ثمود قدار بن سالف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's Messenger was Salih; the warning “God's she-camel and its drink” is an accusative warning to beware harming her, repeated for emphasis like “the lion, the lion.”
rows.anchor: ﴿ فقال لهم رسول الله ﴾ صالح عليه السلام ﴿ ناقة الله ﴾ نصب على التحذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied Salih's warning of punishment and hamstrung the she-camel; the act is attributed to all because they approved it, as in the cited account of their calling their accomplice.
rows.anchor: أى الناقة اسند الفعل اليهم وان كان العاقر واحدا لقوله فنادوا صاحبهم فتعاطى فعقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God annihilated them completely for their denial and hamstringing, making the destruction equal across them so neither child nor adult escaped.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فدمدم عليهم ربهم ﴾ أهلكهم هلاك استئصال ﴿ بذنبهم ﴾ بسبب ذنبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not fear consequences for the act, since no one can hold Him accountable in His dominion as a king might fear reprisal.
rows.anchor: ولا يخاف الله عاقبة هذه الفعلة أى فعل ذلك غير خائف أن تلحقه تبعة من أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Medinese and Syrian readers read “and he does not fear its consequence,” with the pronoun referring to the one who carried out the act.
rows.anchor: فلا يخاف مدنى وشامى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath invokes the one of immense power who created male and female from a single fluid, demonstrating why the oath is binding.
rows.anchor: والقادر العظيم القدرة الذى قدر على خلق الذكروالانثى من ماء واحد وجوب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God undertakes to guide to truth by erecting proofs and explaining revealed laws.
rows.anchor: أن علينا الارشاد إلى الحق بنصب الدلائل وبيان الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the afterlife and present life belong to God, neither misguidance nor guidance benefits Him; alternatively, whoever seeks either from another source has taken the wrong path.
rows.anchor: فلا يضرنا ضلال من ضل ولا ينفعنا اهتداء من اهتدى أو أنهما لنا فمن طلبهما من غيرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning means “I frightened you” of a Fire that blazes fiercely.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فأنذرتكم ﴾ خوفتكم ﴿ نارا تلظى ﴾ نتلهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the most wretched unbeliever, who denied the messengers and turned away from faith, enters the Fire eternally.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لا يصلاها ﴾ لا يدخلها للخلود فيها ﴿ إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The benefactor has no debt of favor to anyone that he must repay; he acts only seeking his Lord's face, and God is exalted in authority and proof, not spatially elevated.
rows.anchor: أى وما لأحد عند الله نعمة يجازية بها إلا أن يفعل فعلا يبتغى به وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse promises pleasing reward that will delight the recipient, as in the promise to the Prophet in al-Duha.
rows.anchor: موعد بالثواب الذى يرضيه ويقر عينه وهو كقوله تعالى لنبية عليه السلام ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife's honored station, Pool, and promised good are better than what pleased the Prophet in worldly life; alternatively, the verse expands the reassurance that God continues revelation and loves him, promising an even greater afterlife rank.
rows.anchor: ما أعد الله لك فى الآخرة من المقام المحمود والحوض المورود والخير الموعود خير مما أعجبك فى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will give the Prophet reward and intercessory standing in the hereafter; when the verse descended, he said he would not be satisfied while even one member of his community remained in the Fire.
rows.anchor: ولما نزلت قال صلى الله عليه وسلم اذا لا أرضى قط وواحد من أمتى فى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām before sawfa is an emphatic lām of initiation, with an implied subject and predicate; it cannot be a lām of oath because that requires an emphatic nūn before a present verb.
rows.anchor: واللام الداخلة على سوف لام الابتداء المؤكدة لمضمون الجملة والمبتدأ محذوف تقديره ولانت سوف يعطيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two emphatic particles combined with delayed fulfillment promise certain giving; earlier blessings are recounted to strengthen hope and patience for still greater good.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن الجمع بين حرفى التأكيد والتأخير يؤذن بأن العطاء كائن لا محالة وان تأخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Did He not find you” uses find in the sense of know, with the two following nouns as its objects; the Prophet was an orphan when his parents died, and his uncle Abu Talib took him in and raised him.
rows.anchor: وهو من الوجود الذى بمعنى العلم والمنصوبان مفعولاه والمعنى ألم تكن يتيما حين مات أبواك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was not yet aware of the prophetic way, revealed law, or matters known through transmitted revelation; God taught him the laws and Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ووجدك ضالا ﴾ أ ى غير عالم ولا واقف على معالم النبوه وأحكام الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says he lost the road to Syria while traveling with Abu Talib and was returned to the caravan; the verse cannot mean that he left truth or committed idolatry, for he was protected from that from childhood until revelation.
rows.anchor: وقيل ضل فى طريق الشام حين خرج به أبو طالب فرده إلى القافلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God found the Prophet poor and enriched him with Khadija's wealth or with spoils God granted him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ووجدك عائلا ﴾ فقيرا ﴿ فأغنى ﴾ فأغناك بمال خديجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not overpower an orphan concerning his property or right because of his weakness.
rows.anchor: فلا تغلبه على ما له وحقه لضعفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not rebuke a petitioner: give something small or answer graciously.
rows.anchor: فلا تزجره فابذل قليلا أو رد جميلا

rows.speaker: السدى
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the petitioner is a seeker of knowledge who comes to the Prophet; he should not be rebuked.
rows.anchor: وعن السدى المراد طالب العلم إذا جاءك فلا تنهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation commands the Prophet to speak of the prophethood God granted him, the greatest blessing; the sounder view encompasses all God's blessings, including teaching Qur'an and religious law.
rows.anchor: أ ى حدث بالنبوة التى آتاك الله وهى أجل النعم والصحيح انها نعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question denies that expansion failed to occur and thereby affirms it; God broadened the Prophet's heart with knowledge and wisdom to bear prophethood and address humans and jinn, removing the constriction of ignorance.
rows.anchor: استفهم عن انتفاء الشرح على وجه الانكار فأفاد اثبات الشرح فكانه قيل شرحنا لك صدرك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet's heart was filled with wisdom and knowledge.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ملئ حكمة وعلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that God lightened the burdens of prophethood; another says the burden was an unspecified lapse, leaving the preferable action while doing the good, for which prophets are reproached and forgiven.
rows.anchor: وخففنا عنك اعباء النبوة والقيام بأمرها وقيل هو زلة لا تعرف بعينها وهى ترك الأفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden weighed on the Prophet until his back made a cracking sound like a joint being strained.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الذي أنقض ظهرك ﴾ أثقله حتى سمع نقيضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's remembrance is elevated by pairing it with God's name in the testimony, call and start of prayer, sermons, tashahhud, Qur'anic commands, and titles such as Messenger of God.
rows.anchor: ورفع ذكره ان قرن بذكر الله فى كلمة الشهادة والآذان والاقامة والخطب والتشهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording first leaves the expanded object implicit and then clarifies it—“your chest,” “your remembrance,” “your burden”—a rhetorical pattern of ambiguity followed by clarification.
rows.anchor: وفائدة ذلك ما عرف فى طريقة الابهام والايضاح لأنه يفهم بقوله ألم نشرح لك أن ثم مشروحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After finishing the call to people, the Prophet should devote himself energetically to worshiping his Lord and link one act of worship to another; the command follows the recounting of past and promised favors by urging gratitude.
rows.anchor: أى فاذا فرغت من دعوة الخلق فاجتهد فى عبادة الرب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the command as striving in supplication after completing prayer; authorities differ whether this is before or after the salutation.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما فإذا فرغت من صلاتك فاجتهد فى الدعاء واختلف أنه قبل السلام أو بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Direct all desire specifically to the Lord, ask no one but His favor, and rely on Him.
rows.anchor: واجعل وغبتك إليه خصوصا ولا تسأل الا فضله متوكلا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sinīn is the region to which Mount Sinai is annexed; like Sinin, it permits inflection with wāw and yāʾ or retention of yāʾ while the nūn takes case endings.
rows.anchor: أضيف الطور وهو الجبل إلى سينين وهى البقعة ونحو سينون بيرون فى جواز الاعراب بالواو والياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure city is Mecca; its trustworthiness is that it protects whoever enters, like a trustworthy person protecting what is entrusted to him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وهذا البلد ﴾ يعنى مكة ﴿ الأمين ﴾ من أمن الرجل أمانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath honors blessed regions through the good brought by prophets and saints: the fig and olive are associated with Abraham's migration and Jesus's birth and upbringing, Sinai with Moses's call, and Mecca with the House, Muhammad's birth, and his mission.
rows.anchor: ومعنى القسم بهذه الأشياء الابانة عن شرف البقاع المباركة وما ظهر فيها من الخير والبركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the first two oath objects indicate where revelation came to Jesus, the third to Moses, and the fourth to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أو الأولان قسم بمهبط الوحى على عيسى والثالث على موسى والرابع على محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may turn to humanity: after this decisive proof, what causes denial of resurrection? Human creation from a drop, development to maturity, then decline in old age proves the Creator can restore people.
rows.anchor: والخطاب فى ﴿ فما يكذبك بعد بالدين ﴾ للانسان على طريقة الالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the address is to the Messenger: who can accuse him of lying after this proof? Here ma means “who.”
rows.anchor: أو لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فمن ينسبك إلى الكذب بعد هذا الدليل فما بمعنى من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing question is a threat to unbelievers: God will judge them according to what they deserve.
rows.anchor: وعيد للكفار وأنه يحكم عليهم بما هم أهله وهو من الحكم والقضاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid are reported to say that al-Alaq was the first surah revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد هى أول سورة نزلت

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority instead say that al-Fatiha was first revealed, followed by al-Qalam.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أن الفاتحة أول ما نزل ثم سورة القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “in the name of your Lord” is an accusative circumstantial phrase: read beginning with God's name, as if instructed first to say the basmala and then read.
rows.anchor: محل باسم ربك النصب على الحال أى اقرأ مفتحا باسم ربك كانه قبل قل بسم الله ثم اقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “created” is omitted either because the phrase means the sole source of creation, or because it means that He created everything, without reason to privilege one creature.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر لخلق مفعولا لأن المعنى الذى حصل منه الخلق واستأثر به لا خالق سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is singled out from all created things because of its nobility and because revelation is directed to it; alternatively, the initially vague “created” is explained afterward to magnify human creation and its wondrous nature.
rows.anchor: تخصيص للانسان بالذكرمن بين ما يتناوله الخلق لشرفه ولأن التنزيل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “clots” is used instead of the singular because the word “human” has a collective sense.
rows.anchor: وإنما جمع ولم يقل من علقه لأن الانسان فى معنى الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Most Generous has perfect generosity beyond every generous being, grants blessings to servants, and delays punishment despite their unbelief and denial; teaching knowledge is an especially profound generosity.
rows.anchor: الذى له الكمال فى زيادة كرمه على كل كريم ينعم على عبادة النعم ويحلم عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught writing by means of the pen.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الذي علم ﴾ الكتابة ﴿ بالقلم ﴿

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's teaching humanity what it did not know demonstrates His generosity, transfers people from ignorance to knowledge, and highlights the benefit of writing, which preserves learning, wisdom, and ancient reports.
rows.anchor: فدل على كمال كرمه بأنه علم عباده ما لم يعلموا ونقلهم من ظلمة الجهل إلى نور العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No indeed” rebukes the person who responds to God's favor with transgression; although he is not named, the context identifies him. The verse through the end of the surah was revealed about Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كلا ﴾ ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله عليه بطغيانه وان لم يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He sees himself” means he knows himself to be self-sufficient; the mental verb can take the two pronouns together, unlike physical seeing.
rows.anchor: أن رأى نفسه يقال فى أفعال القلوب رأيتنى وعلمتنى ومعنى الرؤية العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return is a threat to the transgressor: he will return to his Lord and be repaid for his transgression.
rows.anchor: تهديد للانسان من عاقبة الطغيان على طريق الالتفات والرجعى مصدر بمعنى الرجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who forbids a servant from praying is Abu Jahl attempting to stop Muhammad from prayer.
rows.anchor: أى أرأيت أبا جهل ينهى محمدا عن الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical asks whether the one doing the forbidding follows a sound path in the worship of God that he is trying to prevent.
rows.anchor: أى ان كان ذلك الناهى على طريقة سديدة فيما ينهى عنه من عبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative asks whether he commands righteousness and piety in what he advocates—worship of idols, as he supposes.
rows.anchor: أو كان آمرا بالمعروف والتقوى فيما يأمر به من عبادة الأوثان كما يعتقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question also asks whether this forbidding person denies the truth and turns away from it.
rows.anchor: أرأيت ان كان ذلك الناهى مكذبا بالحق متوليا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees and knows the forbiddener's guidance or error and will repay him accordingly; the first rhetorical question and conditional clauses serve as the two objects of “Have you seen?”, with the conditional answer elided and the second question repeated for emphasis.
rows.anchor: ويطلع على أحواله من هداه وضلاله فيجازيه على حسب حاله وهذا وعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke stops Abu Jahl from forbidding worship of God and commanding idols; if he persists, God will seize him by the forelock and drag him toward imprisonment in the Fire. The written final alif reflects pause.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كلا ﴾ ردع لأبى جهل عن نهيه عن عبادة الله وأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A lying, sinful forelock” apposes the earlier forelock and attributes its owner's lying and sin to it figuratively, a more forceful expression than describing the person directly.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ناصية ﴾ بدل من الناصية لأنها وصفت بالكذب والخطأ بقوله ﴿ كاذبة خاطئة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadi is the gathering place and means its people; zabaniya are the punishment angels, a word for enforcers derived from pushing.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فليدع ناديه سندع الزبانية ﴾ النادى المجلس الذى يجتمع فيه القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abu Jahl confronted the Prophet during prayer, the Prophet rebuked him, and Abu Jahl boasted that he had the largest assembly in the valley; the Prophet warned that the angels would seize him if he called them.
rows.anchor: روى أن أبا جهل مر بالنبى عليه السلام وهو يصلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke is directed at Abu Jahl; the Prophet must persist in disobeying him, continue the prayer and prostration, and draw near to God, for the servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كلا ﴾ ردع لأبى جهل ﴿ لا تطعه ﴾ أى اثبت على ما أنت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “it” exalts the Qur'an by attributing its revelation to God without naming it again; the verse also elevates the time of revelation.
rows.anchor: عظم القرآن حيث اسند انزاله إليه دون غيره وجاء بضميره دون اسمه الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the whole Qur'an descended from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree, then Gabriel conveyed it to the Prophet over twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: روى أنه أنزل جملة فى ليلة القدر من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السماء الدنيا ثم كان ينزله جبريل على رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Night of Decree may mean the night when affairs are measured and decreed, or the night whose exalted rank surpasses other nights.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ليلة القدر ليلة تقدير الأمور وقضائها والقدر بمعنى التقدير أو سميت بذلك لشرفها

rows.speaker: أبى بن كعب
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa reports through Asim and Dharr that Ubayy ibn Ka'b swore the Night of Decree was the twenty-seventh night of Ramadan; the source says this is the majority view.
rows.anchor: روى أبو حنيفة رحمه الله عن عاصم عن ذرأن أبى بن كعب كان يحلف على ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night may be concealed so seekers worship many nights in hope of finding it, as the middle prayer, greatest name, Friday's response-hour, divine pleasure, and anger are concealed; a report recommends asking God for pardon.
rows.anchor: ولعل الداعى إلى اخفائها أن يحي من يريدها الليالى الكثيرة طلبا لموافقتها وهذا كاخفاء الصلاة الوسطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question tells the Prophet that his knowledge had not reached the utmost measure of the Night of Decree's virtue; the next verse explains it.
rows.anchor: أى لم تبلغ درايتك غاية فضلها ثم بين له ذلك بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night surpasses a thousand months that contain no Night of Decree; its excellence comes from the descent of angels and Gabriel and the determination of every wise affair.
rows.anchor: ليس فيها ليلة القدر وسبب ارتقاء فضلها إلى هذه الغاية ما يوجد فيها من تنزل الملائكة والروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet mentioned an Israelite who bore arms in God's path for a thousand months; believers felt their own deeds inadequate and were granted this night, better than that period.
rows.anchor: وذكر فى تخصيص هذه المدة أن النبى عليه السلام ذكر رجلا من بنى إسرائيل فبس السلاح فى سبيل الله ألف شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels descend to the lowest heaven or to earth; “the Spirit” may be Gabriel, a class of angels unseen by other angels that night, or mercy.
rows.anchor: ﴿ تنزل الملائكة ﴾ إلى السماء الدنيا أو إلى الأرض ﴿ والروح ﴾ جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They descend with their Lord's permission concerning each matter He decreed for that year through the next; the phrase marks a stopping point in recitation.
rows.anchor: أى تنزل من أجل كل أمر قضاه الله لتلك السنة إلى قابل وعليه وقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Peace, it is” may mean the night is wholly safety and goodness rather than adversity, or that angels repeatedly greet believing men and women.
rows.anchor: ما هى إلاسلامة خبر ومبتدأ أى لا يقدر الله فيها إلا السلامة والخير

rows.speaker: على وخلف
rows.claim: Ali and Khalaf read the noun with kasra on the lām; the time extends until dawn, while unbelievers are deprived of the night's peace.
rows.anchor: أى إلى وقت طلوع الفجر وبكسر اللام على وخلف وقد حرم من السلام الذين كفروا
